Params: Time flows on, and the pale gray figure never shows up again.
In the beginning, Adelyde still goes to that training room late at night, practicing while hoping for the phantom's return.
But soon the Atlantic Eye consumes her, with studies, experiments, and the daily grind filling every hour. She stops waiting for that miracle, and life proves that none are needed.
Still, whenever she passes an empty doorway, she cannot help but pause for a beat longer than usual.
Several Years Later\nHelio Headquarters, Atlantic Eye

The air ripples with heat beneath a sun faithfully recreated by the holographic simulation. At the center of the circular colosseum, where its arches curve back on themselves, a girl leans heavily on her blade, breathing in ragged gasps. She bites the tip of her tongue hard and forces her body to straighten.
Across the arena, the woman with the imposing frame arches an eyebrow and gives her own shoulder a light tap with the back of her sword.
Hah. Not bad. This is the first time you've held your ground against me for a full hour.
But endurance and technique are just the price of admission.
She traces a shape in the air with her finger, and a cold glint flickers across both blades. The girl freezes for an instant.
In that same heartbeat, the woman's edge cuts toward her student's face, swift and ruthless, with not a trace of leniency.
The blades connect with a brittle crack, and the force drives Adelyde a step backward. She looks up sharply, only to see the next blow hurtling down at her skull.
Survival and battle reflex merge into one motion. She drives forward in a sudden thrust, and blood splatters from the gash she leaves behind.
Rusalka brushes her fingers across the bleeding shoulder and gives a smile that holds no warmth.

All those spineless bureaucrats out there trying to replace our family forces with hired guns are still debating whether training should include simulated casualties. They've never seen real combat a day in their lives.

The Great Family Council put a double-dealing fox into the World Government, then fell for his line that you can buy power with coin. Handed over the vaults themselves. You tell me, what did they do wrong?
She has no intention of letting Adelyde think in silence. The sword hilt spins in her grip, and she unleashes another wave of relentless attacks upon her student.
First... they didn't think far enough.
The girl steadies her breath as she parries each blow. Her thoughts begin to align, and her defenses gradually recover their lost rhythm.
Mercenaries seem like a quick fix for the family's strength, but they go to the highest bidder. And our biggest rival just happens to be our biggest partner right now.
Second, they handed over the initiative.
You never let someone else decide what power you're allowed to hold.
She uses Rusalka's upward slash as a pivot, leaping in the air and bringing her blade down with full force, transforming her defense into a fierce counterattack.
(I can't beat her in strength, so I'll have to beat her in speed!)

Adelyde does not bother counting. Though cuts and bruises stack up on her body, her attacks turn swifter, sharper, more deadly by the moment. And in Rusalka, the old hunger for a worthy fight finally begins to rekindle.
(Maybe someday she'll actually give me a battle worth remembering.)
Rusalka sidesteps a slash that cuts in at a tricky angle, then hurls her longsword with full force. The impact jars Adelyde's grip and knocks the weapon clean from her hands.
Before she can react, Rusalka closes in, clamps a hand around her throat, and slams her onto her back against the floor.
Blood from her wounds runs across the yellow bricks, and only now does Adelyde feel the chill seeping through her body.

Knowledge can be implanted through chips. Technology can be accelerated overnight. But people's hearts don't work like that. If it takes a lifetime to forge a single person's will, what excuse does an entire group have to slack off?
The Cruising Vanguard of the Helio family lets go and straightens up, her gaze fixed on the young contender for family leadership as she struggles to her feet.
Helio commands the energy and infrastructure of the entire TEC, a lifeline and foundation rolled into one. Pull one thread and everything collapses, so you must think comprehensively.
A lifeline and foundation will always attract predators, so you must always strike first.
And above all, remember this, Adelyde: your will is the ultimate killer.
Do not panic when hopeless. Do your best.
Do not budge when cornered. Clear your path.
Do not yield when deadlocked. Ignite your soul.
This era is racing at full throttle. Don't let power that could reshape the world fall into unworthy hands.

The surrounding scene collapses and folds away. Her injuries recede from her skin, inch by inch. The echo of Rusalka's words follows Adelyde as she climbs out of the dark simulation pod and returns to the real world.
Rusalka steps before her and gives her shoulder a firm, approving pat.
I've got an urgent "cleanup job" to handle. Come to my office when I get back. There's something I've been holding onto. It's time to give it to you.
She says no more, pivots on her heel, and strides directly for the door.
Today is the Day of Enlightenment.
Day of Enlightenment marks the first activation of the Atlantic Eye, a holiday established by everyone who took part in its construction.
The celebration, along with the annual planning summit convened the next day by the Great Family Council, both serve to chart the course ahead.
Gathering her courage, the white-haired girl calls out to her teacher, a woman she has never once seen celebrate any holiday.
Isn't that just some holiday the scientists and engineers cooked up for themselves?
Throwing a birthday party for a facility. Ridiculous.
She raises a hand in a backward wave of goodbye, and her figure vanishes through the doorway.
Adelyde waits until she is certain Rusalka is out of sight before she lets herself bend forward slowly.
Her vision has been flickering at the edges ever since she stepped out. Her limbs are heavy and numb, and the pain and terror carried back from the simulation now break over her like a tidal surge.
(I can do this. I can do this.)
Breathe in. Breathe out. Breathe in. Breathe out. She forces her ragged lungs to find a slower, steadier rhythm.
Time slips by, measured only in breaths. Then, in the dim light, the personal terminal she left at the edge of the training ground blinks to life. A voice message notification appears on the screen.
A voice emerges, casual and almost drowsy, yet as clear and pleasing as a mountain spring.
<size=50>Adelyde, do you copy—? This is Arakna—I need—backup—</size>
The evil Spelmin heiress has kidnapped yours truly for her dastardly plans, heading to Port A054.
If you don't come to the hostage's rescue, she will be...
Ahem... Will be forced to review mathematical physics methods with me all weekend?
What? If you want to send me into the sea, you can just say so, or give me a good kick.
Don't worry, Ade. I can keep her busy until you're done with training.
Just message us when you're ready.
The playback ends, yet the warmth carried in her friends' voices seems to remain suspended in the empty training ground.
Adelyde slowly reaches for the terminal, a faint smile touching her lips. She presses the voice button.
As if the weight that had held her down moments ago is simply carried away on the wind, she takes a step, then quickens her stride.
(I don't want to deal with this right now. Time to vanish.)
Huh? Where'd she go? Was I seeing things...

The white-haired girl applies every reconnaissance and anti-surveillance trick her teacher hammered into her, redirecting them from combat to crowd evasion. In no time, she darts through the side exit and out of the building.
The Atlantic Eye spreads out before her, a vision of both monumental grandeur and exquisite precision.

This underwater metropolis is shielded from the crushing ocean by an energy barrier. Inside, an optical simulation system uses the surrounding seawater as its medium, capable of recreating the surface's day-and-night cycles or shifting to full transparency for an unobstructed view of the deep-sea landscape.

The spires and towers rise like a living coral forest, laced with suspended maglev tracks. The vehicles and machines that traverse them are shaped like marine creatures, their lights pulsing with soft glows, drifting through the water as if alive.
Adelyde steps aboard a Manta-7 transport vessel, which carries her to the high-speed elevator that leads directly to the dam's docking port.
Port A054... The Kelpie is moored right there. That shouldn't be just...
The moment she arrives at the meeting spot, a blur of red and white comes flying toward her face. Adelyde reaches out and catches it, a large bouquet of fully bloomed Bourbon roses.
Not far away, a blue-haired girl with several braids leans against her quiet, steady companion and gives a lazy snap of her fingers.
So? What'd you think of that delivery from Mother Nature?
Accurate angle to block my sight, careful control, not a single petal knocked loose—excellent technique. Which means you definitely had nothing to do with it.
She brushes past the blue-haired girl's protests without a word and faces Helentine, whose quiet smile has been waiting for her all along.
All that finely-honed skill of yours, and you're using it to fuel her wild ideas? You'd be better off spending it on a real spar with me.
Heh. It's good to loosen up every now and then.
I see that look on both your faces. There's more coming, isn't there?
Then I'll make sure to deliver.
Arakna pulls a small metal object from her pocket and tosses it into the air, catching it neatly.
The Kelpie's key? How did you get that?
Someone got a summons from her teacher, freaked out, jumped off the boat, and ran off without even pulling the key. So, who do you think docked it? We did.
We could've given it back right away, but that's way too boring.
Just as the white-haired girl starts to cross her arms, Arakna hooks her own through one of them and breaks into a radiant grin.
Whoever holds the key gets to be captain. Today, I'm naming Helentine my first mate.
As for our workaholic VIP who somehow manages to pack thirty-six hours into a single day, your only job is to hold those roses together.
The ignition key clicks down. From beneath the airborne docking port, a hundred meters above the ocean, the low thunder of an engine rises toward them.
In the glow of sunset, an aggressively styled craft pulls up and hovers before the trio.

This is the Spelmin-Helio joint venture's newest marvel, a high-speed sea-air amphibious airship designed to slice through both sea and sky. Every panel flows in seamless curves, its crimson mirror-finish paint catching fire in the evening light.
The canopy unfolds, and under one of the dark seats, a tiny glittering thing is busy wedging itself further out of sight.
A Huhu? When did it sneak in here?
She pokes the little creature's round body, then pulls it out in one smooth motion and cradles it in her arms.
The creature is a jelly-like ecological sponge, one that makes a sound like "huhu," a happy accident born from bionic research. Today, its kin now work as tiny cleaners all across the Atlantic Eye.
These ecological sponges are usually quite shy. They rarely wander beyond the Atlantic Eye. This one must have lost its way.
If I send it back now, will your families pull you away while I'm gone?
The blue-haired girl hoists the squishy, translucent little ball up and locks eyes with its tiny bead-like gaze, her expression utterly solemn.
Your ears are shorter than the others. I'm calling you "Shorty."
And Shorty, for the sake of getting us to Gardener Island before the Day of Enlightenment fireworks start, you're about to become the first Huhu in history to set sail.
She drops the little ball onto Adelyde's lap, then climbs into the pilot's seat.
Hold on, lab sponges usually want nothing to do with me. I—
There's a first time for everything. Play nice!
Buckle up and hold onto the Huhu. You know Arakna's flying style...

No sooner have the words left her mouth than the Kelpie's engine roars to life. The Huhu that had been fighting to escape Adelyde's arms freezes mid-squirm and instantly reverses direction, clinging tightly to the white-haired girl.
Arakna shoves the throttle all the way forward, and the airship bolts ahead like an arrow released from the bow.
In the rush of weightlessness, Adelyde closes her eyes. Not from fear, but in anticipation of what she will see when she opens them—
Golden sunlight pours across the water, with clouds set ablaze at dusk. A magnificent radiance ignites the line where sea and sky converge, and the world stretches endlessly before them.
Wind whips the girls' hair high into the air. The airship skims the water in a sweeping drift, sending plumes of spray meters into the air while Arakna's laughter cuts through the roar.
She glances back, the colossal dam reflected in her eyes as it looms from the deep.
Adelyde reaches one arm as far forward as she can from the back seat, and together with Helentine, one on each side, they steady the rudder.
By the time the recklessly piloted airship finally screeches to a halt at their destination, even Adelyde, hardened by repeated aerial drills, looks somewhat pale.
Somewhere past the midway point, she even had to take over from Arakna and settle into the pilot's seat herself.
She is the first to jump out, turning back to offer her friends a hand down.
I think... your airship... has a problem with its power steering...
The only problem is you went so hard your arms gave out.
Look, people are already gathering. Let's drop the Huhu off and get to the Wishing Platform before it's too crowded.

It may be an abrupt change of subject, but the sky has truly darkened. The little island, adorned with care, begins to sparkle as its lanterns light up. The breeze carries laughter, casual conversation, and the scattered notes of a band warming up.
This is Gardener Island, one of the family residential islands closest to the Atlantic Eye.

The dam's core operations are kept under strict secrecy, and the undersea city accommodates only the scientific and engineering personnel currently on duty. Their loved ones, rather than face prolonged absence, are placed on these outlying islands under TEC's arrangements, making visits possible.
On the side facing the Atlantic Eye, the Wishing Platform towers above the rest of the island, offering an unmatched view of the Day of Enlightenment fireworks.
Above the plaza leading to the Wishing Platform, a massive virtual screen cycles through its display, currently showing the recruitment video that spread across the world just months ago.
...What shapes this era is not a single equation, not a single blueprint; it is people. People who carry their dreams and give their entire lives to see them realized.
If a catastrophe strikes without warning, who stands to protect those fragile sparks? F.O.S. Military Command College. That is my answer.
A few individuals are never enough to carry a civilization. But a generation can. The voyagers of F.O.S. will depart from here and sail toward the stars.
Oh... F.O.S., huh... I heard even getting a spot in the interview queue takes three years.
The ethos and the facilities are both beyond reproach. It could be a good fit... but my father still prefers me to stay here for now.
Mm... besides, we've got everything worth learning right here, and it comes with fireworks.
It is a good academy, she acknowledges silently. But a Helio heir's path makes no room for it.
Light from the screen spills across their shoulders as they walk, but their steps never falter. After all, the ground beneath them is the center of the world.

By the time the three reach the platform with the flowing crowd, most people have already written their wishes on wooden tags and hung them along the ropes circling the structure. Their prayers are not directed to any deity, but to their coworkers.
Please, please let the B17 desalination module validation report pass this time... I've revised it so many times I can't even recognize the words anymore...
You get one wish a year, and everyone else is writing down their real research bottlenecks, hoping some big name will notice and offer a hand. You're using yours on this?
You know what, I'll take it to save you the wait. Send the file to me tomorrow. I'll walk you through the revisions. The sooner it passes, the sooner we can iterate.

Look at this guy, all happy and everything. But let me tell you, he's got his own reasons. His girlfriend's working with the Copperfields on that ecological restoration project, and right now the whole thing's stuck on water.
If this project of his gets approved and rolled out, he's going to be the hero of the hour when he gets home.
Hey! Don't blurt that out! I... okay, fine. That's... also part of it.
I just feel like here, the stuff I'm working on might actually make a difference.
Right, right, world-changing genius. This place really is full of visionaries.
Not that it's a bad thing. That's what makes the Atlantic Eye what it is.

The people beside them continue chatting as they make their way up to the platform. Arakna has already scribbled her wish on a tag at lightning speed, and Helentine hesitates only a brief moment before doing the same.
Let me guess. Same wish as last year? That your family wouldn't have to work so hard?
And yours is still a starship of your own, I presume, "Captain Arakna"?
The blue-haired girl gives her braids a proud little flick, a gesture that says enough. Then she turns to find Adelyde already studying the hanging tags, her own still unwritten.
Look at us. Two wasted wishes, one blank tag. What a crew. Guess we're just here for the spectacle. Now, let's see what other people are wishing for...
This one's praying for a bigger budget next year. That one couldn't fit their equation on the tag, so they just left a terminal code instead.
This one isn't even a wish; it's a thank-you to the precision instruments they maintain. That's actually quite nice.
The two of them notice Adelyde holding a tag, her face briefly going still. Then, with a complicated expression, she puts it back.
That one said something about confessing to Professor Dominik in person. The details are... I'll spare you the details.
Even as her friends drag her up to the top of the Wishing Platform, the blue-haired girl's shoulders keep shaking with laughter.
Quite the writer... though that wish probably isn't coming true any time soon.
Professor Dominik has been rarely seen in public over the past few years. With Project Eden picking up momentum again, I'd imagine his plate is fuller than ever.
Sometimes I wonder what's the bigger miracle. That people put their trust in someone they barely ever see to chart the future, or that his plan is actually coming together?
A light pinch at her side jolts the white-haired girl from her thoughts. She blinks and lifts her gaze back to the present.
Yep, that's the expression. The classic "I have something to say but I'm not sure I should" look.
Whatever it is, just say it. Both of us are here to listen.
I... I don't think it's a miracle.
She steps to the edge of the platform and extends her hand toward the dam's distant, blurred shape.
People believe in him because he has the strength to make good on his promises. And the plan comes together because people have the strength to make good on theirs.
Harnessing the ocean's currents for endless power, steering the climate back on course, bringing the seas back to life... Dominik and Arius are delivering. And so are we.
We're doing all of this, not because we want to, but because we're able to.
So you're saying the world runs on diligence and inevitability, not hope and miracles?
What if it's something beyond your power to change?
Many great feats began simply because someone wanted it very badly.
She shapes her hand into a pretend microphone and lifts it to her chest with theatrical solemnity.
Take me, for example, the TEC's future greatest interstellar explorer. Years from now, when I'm facing the press, I'll look back and say:
My legendary voyage began the day I kidnapped two completely insufferable friends who spent a festival debating philosophy!
As if to drive her words home, the clock chimes the hour, and the entire crowd stretches their necks toward the distant skyline.
Stars...! Stars are rising from the water!
They really are! And they're flying to us!
Far off, countless points of light break through the dark waves, trailing golden streaks as they soar skyward.
They connect in midair one after another, spreading like rippling sheets of light across the heavens. At their peak, they burst into a single, blazing spectacle of fireworks.
The grand display pours down like a waterfall of flame, flooding the sky with brilliance.
...The Comet patrol units? The ones that guard the dam?
The crowd roars with delight as Adelyde looks up, stunned. The fireworks are being launched by autonomous battle drones, machines designed to destroy warships, now painting the sky with light.
A warm, boisterous laugh cuts through the noise, and a woman in engineer's uniform steps forward, speaking to them like old friends.
See the brightest one? Third row from the top, far left. That's mine. I call it Aristo, same as my son.
So, what do you think of the annual calibration run? Launch, formation, detonation, all by the book. You girls like it?
How did you bring the whole Comet team around to this idea, ma'am?
You don't need to convince people to have fun.
Treasure this time, girls, while you can still follow where your heart leads.
"Mankind wanted to rise toward the stars, to write its story in glass and in stone."
The woman gives them a light pat and heads back to her own group, humming a tune under her breath.
So you hold on too... to that part of you that wants to protect something with everything it's got.
So you hold on too... to that part of you that wants to protect something with everything it's got.
Amid the thunder of the countdown fireworks, Adelyde draws a deep breath and tugs her two friends close, ensuring they can hear her above the din.
Can I still make a wish?
I want to protect your wishes.
I want us to still be here, watching fireworks together.
Three! Two! One! Happy Day of Enlightenment!
The three girls lean their heads together and wrap their arms around one another in a tight embrace.
